metaDescription: Seven linear chandeliers compared on length, light count, shade type, dimming, adjustable rods and bulb needs for dining tables and islands, with install notes.
expertTake: The best all-round pick is the 42 in five-light fixture with a stated length and width and glass shades. The value pick is the six-light black fixture at the lowest price tier. Skip a long linear chandelier over a small round table, because a fixture should be about two thirds the table length and a linear shape suits rectangular surfaces.
introParagraphs: A linear chandelier is a bar of lights hung over a rectangular table or a kitchen island, and it replaces the single fixture that never quite reaches the ends of a long surface. In an open plan living and dining space it also defines the dining zone without a wall. The things that decide success are the length against the table, the hanging height and the bulbs.

This guide compares seven linear chandeliers on length, light count, shade type, dimming and adjustable drop. We evaluated each from published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, and we say plainly where a listing gives no wattage limit or no weight. Scores are editorial assessments, not measurements.

products.name: Obihivlo 5-Light Rectangular Linear Chandelier, 42 in Long, Black and Gold
products.description:
This rectangular fixture is 42 in long and 17.4 in wide with five lights, glass shades and a black and gold finish, and the listing states that the hanging height can be adjusted. Having both length and width published is the first thing to look for on a linear fixture, because the width decides how it sits over a table. Five lights give decent output without the weight of a larger fixture.

The tradeoff is that a 42 in fixture suits a table of roughly 60 to 72 in, and over a smaller table it will look oversized. Compared with the 55 in Kwpcvz fixture, it is more modest and easier to place. Glass shades give a bright look, but a clear or seeded shade shows the bulb, so choose warm LED bulbs.

In a real home, hang the bottom of the fixture about 30 to 36 in above the table, and check the ceiling box can carry its weight. Use LED bulbs of modest wattage and turn off the breaker before wiring. Wipe the glass monthly. It suits a rectangular dining table in an open living space. Set the dimmer low for dinner and high for homework, since one fixture then serves both.
products.bestFor: Rectangular dining tables in open living spaces that need a stated-size fixture.

products.name: Boncoo 6-Light Black Linear Chandelier, 32.4 in Long, Adjustable Height
products.description:
This farmhouse island light is 32.44 in long with six lights, a black finish and an adjustable height with easy installation, per the listing. Six lights in a compact length mean a lot of output per inch. It is the cheapest fixture in the comparison.

The tradeoff is that six bulbs in 32 in make a dense, warm cluster that can feel busy, and six sockets mean six bulbs to replace. Compared with the Obihivlo, it is shorter and cheaper. A short fixture suits a small table or island.

For ownership, fit warm LEDs and check the ceiling box. It suits a small island or table where budget matters. Because the fixture is short, a pair of them end to end can cover a longer island.
products.bestFor: Small islands and tables that want high output at the lowest price.

products.name: homary 51.2 in Gold Linear Chandelier with Glass Globes, Stepless Dimming
products.description:
This long gold fixture is 51.2 in with glass globes, stepless dimming and integrated 37 W LED chips. Integrated LEDs mean no bulbs to buy, but they also mean the fixture ends when the LED fails. A long length suits a table of 72 in or more.

The tradeoff is exactly that sealed light source: if the driver fails, you replace the fixture. Compared with the Zicbol, it offers smooth dimming and a longer span. Stepless dimming is a real plus in a living-dining room.

For ownership, check the warranty length and keep the receipt. It suits a long table or island where dimming matters. Keep the receipt and the warranty card, because an integrated light source cannot be repaired.
products.bestFor: Long tables and islands where smooth dimming is a priority.

products.name: Zicbol 45.3 in Modern Linear Chandelier, 4 Lights, Milk Glass Globes
products.description:
This fixture is 45.3 in long with four milk glass globes and a brushed gold finish in a mid-century style. Milk glass hides the bulbs and gives a soft glow. Four lights across 45 in give a calm, even spread.

The tradeoff is output: four milk globes give less light than five or six clear ones, so pair with other sources. Compared with the Obihivlo, it is softer and longer. A mid-century look suits many rooms.

For ownership, fit warm LEDs and wipe the globes. It suits a living-dining area where a gentle glow matters. The globes are glass, so handle the fixture with two people during hanging.

products.name: TinHon 40 in Brass Linear Chandelier with Linen Drum Shades
products.description:
This fixture is 40 in long with linen drum shades and a brushed brass finish. Fabric shades diffuse light and hide the bulbs. A drum shade throws light up and down.

The tradeoff is that fabric can dull and collect dust, and a hot bulb near linen is a risk, so use LEDs. Compared with the glass fixtures, it is softer but less sparkly. The listing gives the dimensions for one shade.

For ownership, dust the shades and use LEDs. It suits a softer, more traditional room. A white or cream shade also reflects some light downward, which helps over a dark table.

This fixture is 39.4 in long and 5.9 in wide with five lights in a modern farmhouse style. A 5.9 in width is slim, so it hangs like a bar over a narrow table or an island. It sits in the middle of the price range.

products.name: Amico 5-Light Seeded Glass Island Chandelier, Farmhouse
products.description:
This five-light fixture has seeded glass shades in a farmhouse style, and the listing says assembly takes about ten minutes. Seeded glass has small bubbles that add sparkle and soften the bulb. It is the second cheapest fixture here.

The tradeoff is that assembly is quick but wiring still needs care, and the data we reviewed gives no dimensions, so check the length before ordering. Compared with the Boncoo, it has glass shades and fewer lights. Seeded glass hides the bulb a little.

For ownership, wipe the glass and check the fixings. It suits a farmhouse dining area. Tighten the shade collars after the first week, because seeded glass shades can loosen as the metal settles.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A fixture should be roughly two thirds the length of the table, and at least 12 in narrower than its width so heads do not bump it. A 42 in fixture suits a 60 to 72 in table. The mistake is hanging a short fixture over a long table, which leaves the ends dark. Measure from the table's end to the fixture's end, not just the lengths, so overhang is even.

Hang the bottom of the fixture 30 to 36 in above the table for 8 ft ceilings, and a little higher for taller ceilings. Adjustable rods let you set the drop. A fixture hung too low blocks conversation and one too high loses its light on the table. If sightlines to a television matter, hang higher and choose a slimmer bar.

Five or six lights give strong output, four soft output. Count the lumens, not the sockets, and use warm LED bulbs. A dimmer on the circuit lets you balance eating and relaxing. Warm light at 2700K flatters food and faces better than a cool white.

Clear and seeded glass sparkle but show bulbs, milk glass is soft, and fabric diffuses. Choose by how you want the light to look. Fabric needs LEDs because of heat. A shade that shows the bulb is best at or above eye level.

Integrated LEDs, as on the homary, never need new bulbs but end the fixture when they fail. Sockets let you swap bulbs. A longer warranty is a practical durability signal. A replaceable bulb is a safer long-term bet than a sealed chip.

A long fixture is heavy, so the ceiling box must be rated for it. Turn off the breaker before wiring and ask an electrician if unsure. No listing here gives a box rating. Ask an electrician to check the box if the fixture is heavier than the old one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated dimensions
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each listing states length and width. The Obihivlo, Boncoo and KSANA do. Missing figures count against a pick. Length and width are the numbers that decide fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Shade and light quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared glass, seeded, milk and fabric shades for comfort. Softer shades score higher in living-dining rooms. Scores are editorial. We did not measure brightness.

howWeEvaluated.description: We noted whether listings state bulb needs or dimming. Clear detail earns credit. We could not verify output. Stepless dimming earned extra credit.

cards.label: Glass
cards.text: Bright and sparkly, easy to wipe. It shows bulbs unless frosted or milk.

cards.label: Fabric
cards.text: Soft and diffused, with a warm look. It collects dust and needs LEDs.

howToChoose.note: Choose glass for sparkle and fabric for softness. Many dining areas suit one of each in different spots.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A dimmable fixture, soft shades and a length that defines the dining zone. Avoid glare in the sightline from the sofa.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The homary has stepless dimming and the Zicbol has milk glass. Both suit open-plan rooms.

howToChoose.note: Put the fixture on a dimmer switch. Add table lamps for the sofa so the chandelier is not the only light.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want smooth dimming, a long span or a stated width, as the homary and Obihivlo offer.

cards.label: Save if

howToChoose.note: Prices move, so compare current listings. Check the length against the table before paying for extras.

maintenance.why: Dust dims glass and dulls fabric. A dry microfibre cloth keeps it clear. Switch the light off and let it cool first.
Hot or loose bulbs can scorch sockets. Use LEDs and replace any that flicker. Warm white LEDs suit dining areas best.
Rods and canopies loosen. Tighten them to avoid sag. Use a ladder with a helper.
A loose canopy exposes wiring. Tighten it with the power off. Turn off the breaker before touching any wires.
Gold and black show fingerprints. A dry cloth keeps them clean. Avoid abrasive cloths on plated finishes.

faq.q: How long should a linear chandelier be?
faq.a: About two thirds the table length. A 42 in fixture suits a table of 60 to 72 in. Also leave about 12 in between the fixture's ends and the table's ends.

faq.q: How high should I hang it?
faq.a: About 30 to 36 in above the table for standard ceilings. Adjust for height. Use the adjustable rods to fine-tune the height after hanging.
A hardwired fixture needs a rated ceiling box and the power off. Ask an electrician if unsure. Never work on live wires.
Yes, with dimmable LED bulbs or an integrated dimmable fixture. Match bulb and dimmer. Check the box on the bulb pack says dimmable.

faq.q: How many lights do I need?
faq.a: Five or six give strong output, four give softer light. Judge by lumens. A dimmer lets you use fewer bulbs at lower brightness.
Many last years if the finish is wiped and fixings checked. No independent source documents lifespan. A longer warranty is a practical durability sign.
